title: Trump reinstated a Schedule Policy/Career category for certain policy roles
description_short: Trump reinstated a Schedule Policy/Career category for certain policy roles
description_medium: Executive Order 14171, signed January 20, 2025, directed a modified Schedule F-style classification for certain confidential or policy-influencing federal positions, later called Schedule Policy/Career. OPM says covered jobs remain career positions filled through merit-based procedures but are not subject to the same removal procedures. The order does not make every federal employee an at-will presidential appointee.
description_long:
On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14171, restoring a modified Schedule F-style category for federal positions with confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating duties. The order reinstated the prior Schedule F policy with amendments, including renaming the category Schedule Policy/Career, and directed OPM to revise implementing regulations. It addresses a defined class of policy-influencing roles; it does not reclassify the entire federal workforce or make every federal employee an at-will presidential appointee.

OPM later finalized a rule establishing Schedule Policy/Career in the excepted service. OPM said the category retains career status and merit-based hiring, including veterans’ preference, while changing the removal procedures that apply to covered positions. The agency also said the rule preserves whistleblower protections and prohibits political patronage, loyalty tests, and political discrimination. OPM’s notice said the rule was published for public inspection on February 5, 2026, takes effect 30 days after publication, and that specific positions may be placed into the category by subsequent presidential executive orders after the rule takes effect.

The cited order and agency notice do not establish how many jobs were ultimately designated or the effect on any individual employee.
previous_description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14171, directing a modified classification for certain federal positions involving confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating duties. OPM later implemented the category as Schedule Policy/Career and said covered roles remain career positions filled through merit-based procedures, including veterans’ preference, while no longer receiving the same removal procedures. The order created a process for identifying positions; it did not itself reclassify every federal employee or grant the president at-will authority over the entire workforce. The available sources do not establish how many positions were ultimately designated or how the rule affected individual employees.

supports: Executive Order 14171 is dated January 20, 2025 and reinstates Executive Order 13957, subject to amendments.
The amendments rename the excepted-service schedule Policy/Career and direct OPM regulatory revisions for specified confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating positions.
limits: The order describes a process and defined class of roles; it does not establish the number of positions ultimately designated or individual employee outcomes.

supports: OPM announced a final rule establishing Schedule Policy/Career in the excepted service for a limited set of policy-influencing positions.
OPM says covered positions remain career roles filled through merit-based procedures, including veterans’ preference, with changed removal procedures.
OPM says the rule preserves whistleblower protections and prohibits political patronage, loyalty tests, and political discrimination.

OPM says the rule was published for public inspection February 5, 2026, takes effect 30 days after publication, and permits specific positions to be placed in the category by presidential executive order after the effective date.
limits: The announcement does not identify the final number of positions designated or document effects for specific employees.
